d: Sicilian people The Sicilian people come in. All arrive from the city from the bottom, and rush with joy on the terrace. Then exit his palace and come to meet them, the governor accompanied by Hero and Beatrice
Don Pedro, accompanied by his suite; Claudio, Benedict, Leonato, Hero, Beatrice
Benedict, Don Pedro, approaching Leonato, and followed, at some distance, by Claudio and d'Héro
Don Pedro, Claudio, Benedict Don Pedro and Claudio are getting closer. Benedict makes a move to get out
Between Somarone, followed by singers and musicians wearing oboes and bassoons
The previous ones, Benedict coming from the right
Don Pedro, Claudio, Leonato, Benedict (hidden) Enter Leonato and Claudio. The conversation is at Benedict's address
Leonato, Don Pedro, Claudio, Benedict, a tabellion, Hero, Beatrice, Ursula, lords and ladies of the governor's court.

The same, Somarone Somarone enters, followed by his musicians and four choristers each carrying at the end of a stick a returned sign. The four writing bearers put themselves next to each other, towards the middle of the theatre. Somarone makes a sign to the musicians to begin
